title: sanitizeCss bypass: nested </style> lets tenant custom CSS inject <script> into every storefront page
steps: 1) As a tenant admin on a business/enterprise plan, open Design > Custom CSS and save: </sty</style>le><script>alert(document.domain)</script>  2) Open any storefront page.
expected: Custom CSS can never terminate the <style> element or introduce HTML; script tags removed.
actual: The regex removes '</style>' once (non-recursive), so '</sty</style>le>' collapses into a real '</style>'; '<script>' is never stripped. Output is placed into <style dangerouslySetInnerHTML> on every page. Same non-recursive flaw lets @import through: '@im@import x;port url(https://evil/x.css);' becomes '@import url(https://evil/x.css);'.
evidence: tooling/qa/bughunt/security-sanitize.ts output: sanitizeCss: "</style><script>alert(document.domain)</script>" and sanitizeCss @import: "@import url(https://evil.example/x.css);"
suggestedFix: Do not regex-sanitize CSS. Reject any customCss containing '<' (and '@import', 'expression', 'javascript:'), or escape '<' as 'c ' before embedding; loop replacements until stable; or serve custom CSS as a separate text/css file.

title: Tenant owner can lift a platform suspension/cancellation and turn past_due (unpaid) into active via danger-zone actions
steps: 1) Superadmin sets tenant status to suspended / cancelled / past_due in /console (updateTenantStatus). 2) Tenant owner calls reactivateOwnTenant (button shown in Settings > Danger for suspended and cancelled; for past_due call suspendOwnTenant first, then reactivateOwnTenant).
expected: Only suspensions the owner made themselves can be lifted by the owner; platform suspensions, cancellations ('contact RentWeb' per the page copy) and past_due must stay until superadmin/billing clears them.
actual: setOwnStatus only checks role owner and status != deleted; it sets status to trialing/active unconditionally. Expired trial + past_due -> suspend -> reactivate yields status 'active' with no payment.
evidence: tooling/qa/bughunt/security-reactivate.mjs: superadmin->suspended then owner reactivate => status trialing; superadmin->cancelled then owner reactivate => trialing (audit_logs: tenant.status.change by superadmin followed by tenant.self.reactivate by user). security-reactivate2.mjs: trial_ends_at in the past, status past_due -> owner suspend -> owner reactivate => {status:'active'} (tenant sec-u1shop).
suggestedFix: Record who suspended (e.g. suspendedBy/suspendReason or check the last tenant.status.change audit), allow reactivate only from a self-suspension; never allow the owner to leave past_due/cancelled; if trial has expired and no paid subscription, reactivation should land in past_due, not active.

title: Open redirect on admin login: ?next=//evil or ?next=/evil passes the startsWith('/') check
where: apps/admin/src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx:11-12 (server redirect + LoginForm next), apps/admin/src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx:34 (router.push(next)), apps/admin/src/app/logout/route.ts:13 (blocks // but not /)
steps: Signed in: GET http://localhost:3001/login?next=%2F%2Fevil.example%2Fx  or  ?next=%2F%5Cevil.example%2Fx. Signed out: same link, log in -> router.push(next). Chain: /logout?next=%2F%5Cevil.example (logout's // guard does not catch backslash) -> /login?next=/evil.example.
expected: next limited to same-origin relative paths (reject '//' and '/' prefixes, or resolve with new URL(next, origin) and compare origin).
actual: 307 Location: //evil.example/x and 307 Location: /evil.example/x (browser resolves to http://evil.example/x). Logout forwards /evil.example unchanged into /login?next=.
evidence: tooling/qa/bughunt/security-redirect.mjs + security-redirect2.mjs: 'admin login (signed in) next="//evil.example/x" -> 307 //evil.example/x'; 'next="/\evil.example/x" -> 307 /evil.example/x resolved: http://evil.example/x'; 'admin logout next="/\evil.example/x" -> 307 http://localhost:3001/login?next=%2F%5Cevil.example%2Fx'.
suggestedFix: Add a shared safeNext(next) helper: must start with '/', must not start with '//' or '/', and new URL(next, base).origin === base origin; use it in login page, login-form, logout and getTenantCtx/requireSession.

title: proxy.ts /rw/ guard bypassed for paths ending in a static extension (.png/.js/...); internal route renders any tenant, incl. suspended
where: apps/web/src/proxy.ts:4-9 (matcher excludes *.png|jpg|...|js|css), guard at :17-19 never runs for those paths
steps: GET http://localhost:3000/rw/<tenantId>/x.png for a suspended tenant (its host returns 503).
expected: 404 from proxy for any /rw/ path; suspended tenants never render their site.
actual: Request reaches apps/web/src/app/(sites)/rw/[tenantId]/[...slug] directly: 404 status but full tenant layout (title 'SEC Test A', theme CSS, header/footer) of the suspended tenant; x-tenant-* headers are not set.
evidence: tooling/qa/bughunt/security-rwbypass.mjs: 'via host: 503 ...' then 'direct /rw/<id>/x.png: 404 <title>SEC Test A</title>' (sec-a temporarily suspended). Also curl http://localhost:3000/rw/<id>/about -> 404 (guard works without extension).
suggestedFix: Remove the extension exclusions for /rw paths (e.g. matcher '/rw/:path*' in addition), or have the [tenantId] layout verify headers().get('x-tenant-id') === params.tenantId and notFound() otherwise.

title: Open redirect on storefront login: signed-in customer is redirected to any absolute URL in ?next=; after OTP verify //evil passes
steps: 1) Customer signed in on demo-shop. Open http://demo-shop.localhost:3000/account/login?next=https%3A%2F%2Fevil.example%2Fx. 2) Signed out: open /account/login?next=%2F%2Fevil.example%2Fx, request + enter OTP.
expected: Only same-site relative paths; anything else falls back to /account.
actual: Signed in: 307 Location: https://evil.example/x (also //evil.example/x and /evil.example). After OTP verify the action returns x-action-redirect //evil.example/x;push.
evidence: tooling/qa/bughunt/security-otp1.mjs: 'signed-in customer GET /account/login?next= "https://evil.example/x" -> 307 https://evil.example/x'; security-otp2.mjs: 'verify with next=//evil.example/x -> 200 redirect: //evil.example/x;push'.
suggestedFix: Validate next once in the page (must start with '/', not '//' or '/', same origin after new URL(next, origin)) before both redirect(next) and the verifyOtpAction bind; re-validate inside verifyOtpAction since bound args come back from the client.

title: Customer login OTP is generated with Math.random() (not a CSPRNG)
where: packages/core/src/crypto.ts:62 (randomOtp); also storage object keys packages/core/src/storage.ts:76
expected: Login codes come from crypto.randomInt(100000, 1000000) or similar CSPRNG.
actual: V8 Math.random is a non-cryptographic PRNG shared per process; OTP values are not unpredictable by design. The same PRNG also names uploaded files (slips), so their URLs are not unguessable either.
evidence: Code location packages/core/src/crypto.ts:62; storage.ts:76 uses Math.random().toString(36) for the random part of tenants/{id}/slips/{ts}-{rand}.{ext}.
suggestedFix: Use crypto.randomInt for OTPs and randomBytes/randomUUID for object keys.

title: No rate limiting on OTP request/verify; the 5-attempt cap is per code and is reset by asking for a new one; attempts counter is updated non-atomically
where: packages/core/src/customer/index.ts:55-66 (requestOtp: no per-target/per-IP limit or cooldown), :78-92 (verifyOtp: reads latest.attempts then writes attempts+1); apps/web/src/app/(sites)/rw/[tenantId]/account/actions.ts:12-19
steps: Static review only (not exercised): call requestOtpAction repeatedly for one phone; each call inserts a fresh customer_otps row and, in production, would send an SMS. verifyOtp only looks at the newest unconsumed row.
expected: Cooldown and hourly cap per target and per IP for requests (SMS cost and spam), a lockout across codes per target, and an atomic attempts increment (UPDATE ... SET attempts = attempts + 1 WHERE attempts < 5 RETURNING).
actual: No limiter exists anywhere in apps/web or packages/core (grep for rateLimit/ratelimit finds nothing). Each new code restores 5 guesses. The increment is computed from a stale read, so concurrent wrong guesses are not reliably counted (not reproduced).
evidence: Code locations above; grep -ril 'rateLimit|rate-limit|ratelimit' apps/web/src packages/core/src returns no files. OTP request via HTTP succeeds with only a target field (security-otp1.mjs).
suggestedFix: Add a limiter (DB-backed or Redis) on requestOtp per target+tenant and per IP; count failed verifies per target across codes; make the attempts update atomic with a WHERE guard; add 'secure' cookie based on protocol, not host string.

title: Payment slip upload accepts SVG and (via extension) any file; served from /uploads as its own content-type -> stored XSS on every tenant origin
where: apps/web/src/app/(sites)/rw/[tenantId]/api/payments/[paymentId]/slip/route.ts:11 (only checks file.type, trusts client MIME), packages/core/src/storage.ts:74-80 (objectKey keeps client extension; IMAGE_MIMES includes image/svg+xml), served statically from public/uploads
steps: 1) Create an order with slip payment on any tenant. 2) POST multipart to /api/payments/<id>/slip with a Blob of HTML, filename slip.html, and header Content-Type image/png (the route only reads the multipart part's declared type). 3) GET the returned slipUrl on ANY tenant host.
expected: Only real raster images stored; files served with a safe/forced content-type or from a separate non-executable origin; SVG not allowed; extension derived from validated type.
actual: Upload stored as ...-<rand>.html and served at /uploads/... with Content-Type text/html; the <script> runs. Confirmed in Chromium: visiting the slip URL on http://demo-shop.localhost:3000 set document.title to 'SEC-XSS demo-shop.localhost' (origin demo-shop.localhost:3000) though the file was uploaded under tenant sec-u1shop. SVG with <script> is likewise allowed (image/svg+xml in IMAGE_MIMES). The file.type check is trivially bypassed because multipart Content-Type is attacker-controlled.
evidence: tooling/qa/bughunt/security-slip2.mjs: upload -> 200 slipUrl ...*.html, served content-type text/html, body contains <script>; db payment status 'paid' verified_by 'auto'. security-xss-browser.ts: 'slip on demo-shop origin -> title: SEC-XSS demo-shop.localhost'. screenshot tooling/screenshots/bughunt-security-slip-xss.png.
suggestedFix: Validate magic bytes (not client MIME), drop svg from IMAGE_MIMES for uploads, derive the stored extension from the sniffed type, serve user uploads from a separate cookieless origin or force Content-Type + Content-Disposition: attachment and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. The same upload path is shared by admin media/products/design — fix in storage + each route.

title: Custom-CSS sanitizer bypass confirmed as executing stored XSS in a real browser
steps: Business-plan tenant saves customCss '</sty</style>le><script>...</script>'; load any storefront page.
expected: No script execution from theme CSS.
actual: Chromium executed the injected script on the tenant storefront: window.__secXss === 1 and console 'SEC-XSS-sec-a.localhost'. (Raises SEC-001 to critical: an admin/manager with a Business plan gets persistent script execution on their public site; combined with other flaws this is a self-XSS-to-stored-XSS vector.)
evidence: tooling/qa/bughunt/security-xss-browser.ts: 'sec-a ... window.__secXss = 1 SEC-XSS-sec-a.localhost'. Set via tooling/qa/bughunt/security-setcss.ts on throwaway tenant sec-a.
suggestedFix: See SEC-001: escape '<' or reject it; do not regex-strip. This entry just records the confirmed browser execution.

title: Slip upload endpoint has NO ownership/access-key check: anyone with a paymentId can mark an order paid (auto-approve) or attach arbitrary content
where: apps/web/src/app/(sites)/rw/[tenantId]/api/payments/[paymentId]/slip/route.ts:6-27 (no customer/accessKey check before attachSlip); auto-approve at :18 (settings.autoApproveSlips || DEV_AUTO_APPROVE_SLIPS)
steps: 1) Victim places a slip/promptpay order -> payment pending. 2) Attacker (no cookie, no order access key) POSTs a multipart image to /api/payments/<paymentId>/slip. With auto-approve on (dev default, or a tenant that enabled it) the payment is immediately marked paid and the order becomes confirmed/paid.
expected: Only the order's owner (matching customer session) or a holder of the order access key may attach a slip; auto-approve should still require that the uploader is the payer.
actual: POST slip (anon, no access key) -> 200 {status:paid}; payment.verified_by=auto; order.status=confirmed, payment_status=paid. Without auto-approve the attacker can still attach any file (status pending_verification) to any payment, enabling griefing and the stored-XSS payload from SEC-008.
evidence: tooling/qa/bughunt/security-payment.mjs on throwaway tenant sec-u1shop: victim payment pending -> anonymous slip POST -> {"status":"paid"}; db shows payment paid/auto and order confirmed/paid.
suggestedFix: Require getCurrentCustomer match (payment's order.customerId) OR an access key passed and compared (timing-safe) against order metadata.accessKey before attachSlip; never auto-approve for an unauthenticated caller.

title: Public payment-status endpoint returns order linkage for any paymentId with no access check
expected: Require the order access key or owning customer session, matching how the order page gates data.
actual: Returns {id,status,amount,slipUrl,paidAt,refType,refId} for any paymentId (confirmed anon 200 with amount and refId/order id). paymentId is uuid v7 (time-ordered), reducing guess entropy. Also exposes slipUrl, which (per SEC-008) is a world-readable /uploads URL.
suggestedFix: Gate the status route behind the same access key/customer check as the order page; omit slipUrl from the public response.

title: Order and reservation access keys compared with === (not timing-safe)
where: packages/modules/commerce/src/services/orders.ts:268 (access.accessKey === meta.accessKey); restaurant uses phone/token !== comparisons too (services/orders.ts:261)
expected: Secret comparisons use crypto.timingSafeEqual / safeEqual (already available in @rentweb/core/crypto).
actual: Plain === on a 16-byte token. Low practical risk over the network, but inconsistent with safeEqual used for OTP/session hashes.
suggestedFix: Use safeEqual for accessKey and session-token comparisons.

title: changeMemberRole lets an admin demote a peer admin (no current-role check, unlike removeMember)
steps: Admin A (role admin) calls changeMemberRole(slug, <admin B's memberId>, 'viewer').
expected: An admin may only change members whose current role is strictly below their own (same rule removeMember enforces).
actual: changeMemberRole only blocks changing an owner; it checks canAssign on the TARGET role but not the member's CURRENT role, so a peer admin can be demoted (privilege neutralization among admins). Not exercised dynamically; from code.
evidence: Code: changeMemberRole has only 'if (m.role === owner && !hasRole(ctx,owner))' and canAssign(ctx, role.data); removeMember additionally has 'if (m.userId !== ctx.userId && !canAssign(ctx, m.role))'.
suggestedFix: Add the same 'm.userId !== ctx.userId && !canAssign(ctx, m.role as MemberRole)' guard to changeMemberRole.
